question: Choose the antonym of COMPLEX.
reason: Complex means complicated; its opposite is uncomplicated (simple).
why: Complex means having many parts and hard to understand, so its opposite is Uncomplicated (simple, easy). A) Intricate, B) Complicated and D) Puzzling are wrong: they all mean the same as complex, so they are synonyms, not antonyms.
rel: Other antonyms of complex: simple, easy, plain, straightforward. Synonyms: complicated, intricate, involved.

question: Choose the antonym of ACTIVITY.
reason: Activity means being busy or active; its opposite is inactivity.
why: Activity means being busy or moving and doing things; its opposite is Inactivity (doing nothing). A) Energy, C) Movement and D) Action are wrong: they are all close in meaning to activity, not opposite.
rel: Other antonyms: idleness, inertia, rest. The prefix in- makes many opposites: active - inactive, efficient - inefficient.

question: Choose the antonym of LACK.
reason: Lack means shortage; its opposite is abundance (plenty).
why: Lack means not having enough of something; its opposite is Abundance (a lot, more than enough). A) Deficiency, B) Absence and D) Shortage are wrong: they all mean the same as lack.
rel: Other antonyms of lack: plenty, sufficiency, surplus. Synonyms: want, dearth, scarcity.

question: Choose the antonym of MISLEAD.
reason: Mislead means to lead in the wrong direction; its opposite is guide.
why: Mislead means to lead someone the wrong way or give a wrong idea; its opposite is Guide (show the right way). A) Confuse, B) Deceive and D) Misdirect are wrong: they all have the same meaning as mislead.
rel: The prefix mis- means wrongly: misguide, misinform, misunderstand. Antonyms of mislead also include direct and inform correctly.

question: Choose the antonym of PUNCTUAL.
reason: Punctual means on time; its opposite is unpunctual (late).
why: Punctual means arriving on time; its opposite is Unpunctual (late, not on time). A) Regular and D) Careful are wrong: they are not opposites of punctual. B) Prompt is wrong: it is a synonym (on time).
rel: Other antonyms: late, tardy, delayed. Synonyms of punctual: prompt, timely.

question: Choose the antonym of MERRY.
reason: Merry means happy and cheerful; its opposite is sad.
why: Merry means happy and cheerful; its opposite is Sad. B) Cheerful, C) Jolly and D) Lively are wrong: they all mean happy or full of fun, so they are synonyms.
rel: Other antonyms of merry: gloomy, sorrowful, glum. Synonyms: joyful, gay, jovial.

question: Choose the antonym of HUMBLE.
reason: Humble means modest; its opposite is vain (proud, conceited).
why: Humble means modest, not proud; its opposite is Vain (proud of oneself). B) Modest, C) Simple and D) Meek are wrong: they are all close in meaning to humble.
rel: Other antonyms of humble: proud, arrogant, haughty. Note that sa-73 uses Meek as a synonym of humble.

question: Choose the antonym of FLEXIBLE.
reason: Flexible means easily bent or adjusted; its opposite is rigid (stiff).
note: Fixed: source had 'Unplant' (likely 'unpliant'); used standard antonym 'Rigid'.
why: Flexible means easy to bend or change; its opposite is Rigid (stiff, cannot bend). A) Pliable, B) Supple and D) Elastic are wrong: they all mean bendable, so they are synonyms.
rel: Other antonyms of flexible: stiff, inflexible, unbending. Synonyms: pliant, bendable.

question: Choose the antonym of IMAGINARY.
reason: Imaginary means existing only in the mind; its opposite is real.
why: Imaginary means existing only in the mind; its opposite is Real. B) Fanciful, C) Fictional and D) Unreal are wrong: they all mean not real, the same as imaginary.
rel: Other antonyms: actual, factual, existing. Do not confuse imaginary (not real) with imaginative (creative).

question: Choose the antonym of SUPPORT.
reason: Support means to help or stand by; its opposite is abandon (desert).
why: Support means to help or hold up; its opposite is Abandon (leave and stop helping). A) Help, C) Assist and D) Uphold are wrong: they all mean the same as support.
rel: Other antonyms of support: oppose, desert, undermine. Synonyms: back, aid, sustain.

question: Choose the antonym of NERVOUS.
reason: Nervous means anxious or fearful; its opposite is bold (confident).
why: Nervous means worried and afraid; its opposite is Bold (brave, confident). A) Anxious and B) Restless are wrong: they mean worried or uneasy, like nervous. C) Timid is wrong: it means shy and fearful, also close to nervous.
rel: Other antonyms of nervous: calm, confident, composed. In sa-74, Timorous is a synonym of nervous.

question: Choose the antonym of MAJORITY.
reason: Majority means the greater number; its opposite is minority.
why: Majority means the larger part or number; its opposite is Minority (the smaller part). A) Plurality, C) Bulk and D) Mass are wrong: they all refer to the larger part or a big amount.
rel: Same pattern: major - minor, majority - minority. Majority means more than half.

question: Choose the antonym of ATTRACT.
reason: Attract means to pull towards; its opposite is repel (push away).
why: Attract means to pull towards; its opposite is Repel (push away). A) Charm, C) Allure and D) Draw are wrong: they all mean to attract or pull in.
rel: In magnets, like poles repel and unlike poles attract. Noun pair: attraction - repulsion (see sa-25).

question: Choose the antonym of TENDENCY.
reason: Tendency means an inclination towards something; its opposite is disinclination.
why: Tendency means a natural leaning to do something; its opposite is Disinclination (unwillingness). B) Habit, C) Leaning and D) Inclination are wrong: they are all close in meaning to tendency.
rel: Other antonyms: aversion, reluctance, unwillingness. Inclination and disinclination are an opposite pair made with dis-.

question: Choose the antonym of FREEDOM.
reason: Freedom means liberty; its opposite is slavery.
why: Freedom means being free; its opposite is Slavery (being owned or controlled). A) Liberty, C) Release and D) Independence are wrong: they all mean freedom.
rel: Other antonyms of freedom: bondage, captivity, servitude. Synonyms: liberty, independence, autonomy.

question: Choose the antonym of TROUBLE.
reason: Trouble means to disturb or worry; its opposite is appease (calm, pacify).
why: Here trouble is a verb meaning to disturb or worry someone; its opposite is Appease (calm or soothe). A) Disturb, B) Annoy and C) Worry are wrong: they all mean the same as trouble.
rel: Other antonyms of trouble: calm, soothe, comfort, pacify. Appease means to calm someone by giving what they want.

question: Choose the antonym of QUESTIONABLE.
reason: Questionable means doubtful; its opposite is unquestionable (certain).
why: Questionable means doubtful, not certain; its opposite is Unquestionable (certain, beyond doubt). A) Doubtful, C) Dubious and D) Uncertain are wrong: they all mean the same as questionable.
rel: Other antonyms: certain, sure, undeniable, indisputable. Prefix un- makes the opposite: questionable - unquestionable.

question: Choose the antonym of COMFORT.
reason: Comfort means ease and relief; its opposite here is oppression (hardship, distress).
why: Comfort means ease and relief from pain or worry; its opposite is Oppression (hard and cruel treatment, burden). A) Relief, B) Ease and C) Solace are wrong: they all mean comfort.
rel: Other antonyms of comfort: distress, discomfort, misery. Solace means comfort in sadness.

question: Choose the antonym of APPROVAL.
reason: Approval means agreeing or accepting; its opposite is disapproval.
why: Approval means agreeing that something is good or allowed; its opposite is Disapproval. A) Sanction, B) Assent and C) Consent are wrong: they all mean approval or permission.
rel: Other antonyms: rejection, refusal, disapprobation. In sa-64, Consent is a synonym of approval.

question: Choose the antonym of ACCUSATION.
reason: Accusation means a charge against someone; its opposite is defence.
why: An accusation is a charge that someone did wrong; its opposite is Defence (speaking to protect oneself against the charge). B) Allegation, C) Charge and D) Blame are wrong: they all mean the same as accusation.
rel: Accuse (verb) - defend (verb). Other related words: vindication, exoneration (being cleared of blame).

question: Choose the antonym of ACHIEVEMENT.
reason: Achievement means success in doing something; its opposite is failure.
why: Achievement means success in doing something; its opposite is Failure. A) Accomplishment, B) Attainment and C) Success are wrong: they all mean achievement.
rel: Other antonyms: defeat, loss. In sa-60, Accomplishment is a synonym of achievement.

question: Choose the antonym of RAMBLING.
reason: Rambling means wandering without order; its opposite is methodical (orderly).
why: Rambling means talking or writing in a long, wandering, unorganized way; its opposite is Methodical (orderly, organized). A) Disorganized, C) Lengthy and D) Wandering are wrong: they all describe rambling.
rel: Other antonyms: concise, organized, systematic, to the point. Synonyms: digressive, long-winded.

question: Choose the antonym of WILD.
reason: Wild means untamed or savage; its opposite is civilized.
why: Wild means not tamed, savage; its opposite is Civilized. A) Fierce, B) Untamed and C) Savage are wrong: they all mean the same as wild.
rel: Other antonyms of wild: tame, gentle, domesticated. In sa-58, Savage is a synonym of wild.

question: Choose the antonym of WICKED.
reason: Wicked means evil; its opposite is virtuous (good, moral).
why: Wicked means evil or very bad; its opposite is Virtuous (good, moral). A) Cruel, B) Evil and D) Sinful are wrong: they all mean bad, like wicked.
rel: Other antonyms: righteous, noble, good. In sa-57, Evil is a synonym of wicked.

question: Choose the antonym of ATTRACTION.
reason: Attraction means a pulling force or appeal; its opposite is repulsion.
why: Attraction means a pull towards something; its opposite is Repulsion (pushing away, strong dislike). B) Appeal, C) Allure and D) Charm are wrong: they all mean attraction.
rel: Verb pair: attract - repel (see sa-13). Other antonyms: aversion, revulsion.

question: Choose the antonym of DANGER.
reason: Danger means risk of harm; its opposite is safety.
why: Danger means the chance of harm; its opposite is Safety. A) Hazard, C) Risk and D) Peril are wrong: they all mean danger.
rel: Other antonyms: security, protection, shelter. In sa-61, Risk is a synonym of danger.

question: Choose the antonym of EFFICIENCY.
reason: Efficiency means working well without waste; its opposite is inefficiency.
why: Efficiency means doing work well without waste; its opposite is Inefficiency. A) Skill, B) Competence and C) Capability are wrong: they are close in meaning to efficiency.
rel: Prefix in- makes the opposite: efficient - inefficient, capable - incapable, competent - incompetent.

question: Choose the antonym of EXCESS.
reason: Excess means more than needed; its opposite is scarcity (shortage).
why: Excess means more than needed; its opposite is Scarcity (too little). A) Surplus, B) Abundance and D) Plenty are wrong: they all mean a large amount, like excess.
rel: Other antonyms of excess: shortage, deficiency, lack. Synonyms: surplus, glut.

question: Choose the antonym of ABILITY.
reason: Ability means the power to do something; its opposite is incapability.
why: Ability means power or skill to do something; its opposite is Incapability (not being able). A) Capability, B) Skill and C) Talent are wrong: they all mean ability.
rel: Other antonyms: inability, incapacity, incompetence. In sa-43, Capability is a synonym of ability.

question: Choose the antonym of COMPULSORY.
reason: Compulsory means required by rule; its opposite is optional.
why: Compulsory means something you must do; its opposite is Optional (you may choose). B) Mandatory, C) Necessary and D) Obligatory are wrong: they all mean must-do, like compulsory.
rel: Other antonyms: voluntary, elective, discretionary. Synonyms: required, binding.

question: Choose the antonym of ABUSE.
reason: Abuse means insulting or harsh words; its opposite is commendation (praise).
why: Abuse means insulting or harsh words; its opposite is Commendation (praise). A) Insult, B) Reproach and D) Criticism are wrong: they are all close in meaning to abuse.
rel: Other antonyms: praise, respect, honour. In sa-66, Reproach is a synonym of abuse.

question: Choose the antonym of WANT.
reason: Want here means poverty or need; its opposite is prosperity.
why: Here want means poverty or lack of things; its opposite is Prosperity (wealth, having plenty). A) Need, B) Shortage and D) Poverty are wrong: they all mean the same as want.
rel: Other antonyms: plenty, wealth, abundance. Phrase: to live in want means to live in poverty.

question: Choose the antonym of AGREE.
reason: Agree means to have the same opinion; its opposite is disagree.
why: Agree means to have the same opinion; its opposite is Disagree. B) Consent, C) Approve and D) Accept are wrong: they all mean to agree.
rel: Prefix dis- makes the opposite: agree - disagree, approve - disapprove, like - dislike.

question: Choose the antonym of RECOVER.
reason: Recover means to get back; its opposite is lose.
why: Recover means to get back something lost; its opposite is Lose. A) Regain, B) Retrieve and D) Restore are wrong: they all mean getting something back, like recover.
rel: Recover also means to get well after illness; its opposite then is worsen or deteriorate. Synonyms: reclaim, recoup.

question: Choose the antonym of OWN.
reason: Own here means to admit or acknowledge; its opposite is disclaim (deny).
why: Here own means to admit or accept something; its opposite is Disclaim (refuse to accept or deny). A) Admit, B) Accept and D) Acknowledge are wrong: they all mean the same as own.
rel: Other antonyms: deny, disown, reject. In sa-77, Acknowledge is a synonym of own.

question: Choose the antonym of EQUAL.
reason: Equal means the same in amount or value; its opposite is uneven (unequal).
why: Equal means the same in size, amount or level; its opposite is Uneven (not the same). A) Same, B) Uniform and D) Identical are wrong: they all mean alike, like equal.
rel: Other antonyms: unequal, different, unlike. In sa-76, Uniform is a synonym of equal.

question: Choose the antonym of SIN.
reason: Sin means a wrong or immoral act; its opposite is virtue.
why: Sin means a wrong or evil act; its opposite is Virtue (goodness). A) Crime, C) Evil and D) Wrongdoing are wrong: they all mean the same as sin.
rel: Other antonyms: goodness, merit, righteousness. In sa-48, Crime is a synonym of sin.

question: Choose the antonym of PROVE.
reason: Prove means to show something is true; its opposite is disprove.
why: Prove means to show something is true; its opposite is Disprove (show it is false). A) Establish, B) Confirm and D) Verify are wrong: they all mean to prove.
rel: Prefix dis- gives the opposite: prove - disprove, approve - disapprove. Other antonyms: refute, rebut.

question: Choose the antonym of PROGRESS.
reason: Progress means to move forward; its opposite is retrogress (move backward).
why: Progress means moving forward; its opposite is Retrogress (go backward). A) Develop, C) Proceed and D) Advance are wrong: they all mean moving forward, like progress.
rel: Other antonyms: regress, decline, deteriorate. In sa-71, Advance is a synonym of progress.

question: Choose the antonym of FREE.
reason: Free means to release; its opposite is bind (tie up).
why: Free (verb) means to let go; its opposite is Bind (tie up). A) Loosen, B) Liberate and D) Release are wrong: they all mean to set free.
rel: Other antonyms: confine, imprison, fetter, restrain. Bind - bound - bound are its verb forms.

question: Choose the antonym of PRAISE.
reason: Praise means to speak well of; its opposite is censure (strong criticism).
why: Praise means to say good things about someone; its opposite is Censure (strong criticism). B) Admire, C) Laud and D) Applaud are wrong: they all mean to praise or show approval.
rel: Other antonyms: blame, condemn, criticize. In sa-86, Laud is a synonym of praise.

question: Choose the antonym of JUSTICE.
reason: Justice means fairness; its opposite is inequity (injustice, unfairness).
why: Justice means fairness; its opposite is Inequity (unfairness). A) Honesty, C) Equity and D) Fairness are wrong: they are close in meaning to justice.
rel: Do not confuse inequity (unfairness) with iniquity (wickedness). Other antonyms of justice: injustice, unfairness.

question: Choose the synonym of ABILITY.
reason: Ability means the power or skill to do something, the same as capability.
why: Ability means power or skill to do something; its synonym is Capability. B) Weakness, C) Inability and D) Failure are wrong: they are opposite in meaning to ability.
rel: Other synonyms: skill, talent, competence, capacity. Antonym: inability (see sa-29).

question: Choose the synonym of BLAME.
reason: Blame means to hold someone responsible for a fault, similar to censure.
why: Blame means to say someone is responsible for a wrong; its synonym is Censure (criticize strongly). A) Approve, B) Pardon and C) Praise are wrong: they are opposite in meaning to blame.
rel: Other synonyms: condemn, criticize, reproach. Censure is also the antonym of praise (see sa-41).

question: Choose the synonym of EFFICIENCY.
reason: Efficiency means effectiveness or power to produce results, similar to potency.
why: Efficiency means power to do work well; Potency (power, effectiveness) is the closest synonym. B) Weakness, C) Waste and D) Laziness are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.
rel: Other synonyms: effectiveness, competence, capability (see sa-63). Antonym: inefficiency.

question: Choose the synonym of COMPLEX.
reason: Complex means having many connected parts, i.e. complicated.
why: Complex means having many parts and hard to understand; its synonym is Complicated. A) Easy, B) Plain and C) Simple are wrong: they are opposite in meaning to complex.
rel: Other synonyms: intricate, involved, elaborate. Antonym: uncomplicated (see sa-1).

question: Choose the synonym of LACK.
reason: Lack means not having enough, i.e. deficiency.
why: Lack means not having enough; its synonym is Deficiency. A) Abundance, C) Excess and D) Plenty are wrong: they mean a lot, the opposite of lack.
rel: Other synonyms: shortage, want, dearth, scarcity. Antonym: abundance (see sa-3).

question: Choose the synonym of SIN.
reason: Sin means a wrong or immoral act, similar to crime.
why: Sin means a wrong or evil act; Crime (a wrong act) is the closest synonym. B) Goodness, C) Virtue and D) Merit are wrong: they mean good qualities, the opposite of sin.
rel: Other synonyms: wrongdoing, evil, offence, misdeed. Antonym: virtue (see sa-37).

question: Choose the synonym of SILLY.
reason: Silly means lacking good sense, i.e. foolish.
why: Silly means not sensible; its synonym is Foolish. A) Clever, C) Wise and D) Sensible are wrong: they are opposite in meaning to silly.
rel: Other synonyms: stupid, absurd, senseless. Antonyms: wise, sensible, intelligent.

question: Choose the synonym of AGREEABLE.
reason: Agreeable means willing to agree or fit in, similar to conformable.
why: Agreeable means willing to agree or go along; Conformable (fitting in, in agreement) is the synonym. A) Opposed, B) Hostile and D) Contrary are wrong: they mean against, the opposite.
rel: Agreeable also means pleasant (an agreeable person). Other synonyms: compliant, willing, pleasing.

question: Choose the synonym of DECIDE.
reason: Decide means to make up one's mind, i.e. determine.
why: Decide means to make up one's mind; its synonym is Determine. A) Hesitate, B) Waver and C) Doubt are wrong: they all mean being unable to decide.
rel: Other synonyms: resolve, settle, conclude. Noun forms: decision, determination.

question: Choose the synonym of REASON.
reason: Reason (verb) means to think logically or put forward arguments, i.e. argue.
why: As a verb, reason means to think and discuss logically, to argue a point; so Argue is the synonym. B) Ignore is wrong: it means to pay no attention. C) Accede is wrong: it means to agree to a demand. D) Obey is wrong: it means to follow orders.
rel: Phrase: to reason with someone means to try to persuade them by argument. Other synonyms: deduce, infer, think.

question: Choose the synonym of URGE.
reason: Urge means to push someone strongly to act, similar to incite.
why: Urge means to push or strongly encourage; its synonym is Incite (stir up, provoke to action). A) Discourage, B) Deter and C) Restrain are wrong: they mean to stop or hold back, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: prompt, spur, press, impel. Antonyms: deter, dissuade.

question: Choose the synonym of SCOLD.
reason: Scold means to speak angrily to someone for a fault, i.e. reprove.
why: Scold means to speak angrily to someone for doing wrong; its synonym is Reprove. A) Praise, B) Commend and D) Flatter are wrong: they all mean saying good things, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: rebuke, reprimand, chide, admonish. Antonyms: praise, commend.

question: Choose the synonym of DILIGENT.
reason: Diligent means hard-working and careful, i.e. industrious.
why: Diligent means hard-working and careful; its synonym is Industrious. B) Idle, C) Lazy and D) Careless are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.
rel: Other synonyms: hard-working, assiduous, sedulous. Do not confuse industrious (hard-working) with industrial (of industry).

question: Choose the synonym of EMPTY.
reason: Empty means containing nothing, i.e. vacant.
why: Empty means containing nothing; its synonym is Vacant. A) Crowded, B) Full and C) Occupied are wrong: they mean filled, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: void, blank, unoccupied, hollow. Antonyms: full, occupied.

question: Choose the synonym of WICKED.
reason: Wicked means morally bad, i.e. evil.
why: Wicked means very bad; its synonym is Evil. A) Virtuous, C) Kind and D) Noble are wrong: they mean good, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: sinful, vicious, cruel. Antonym: virtuous (see sa-24).

question: Choose the synonym of WILD.
reason: Wild means untamed and fierce, i.e. savage.
why: Wild means untamed and fierce; its synonym is Savage. B) Gentle, C) Civilized and D) Tame are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.
rel: Other synonyms: untamed, fierce, ferocious. Antonym: civilized (see sa-23).

question: Choose the synonym of TENDENCY.
reason: Tendency means a natural inclination, i.e. leaning.
why: Tendency means a natural leaning toward something; its synonym is Leaning. A) Dislike, C) Reluctance and D) Aversion are wrong: they mean not wanting, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: inclination, propensity, bent, trend. Antonym: disinclination (see sa-14).

question: Choose the synonym of ACHIEVEMENT.
reason: Achievement means something done successfully, i.e. accomplishment.
why: Achievement means something done successfully; its synonym is Accomplishment. A) Defeat, B) Failure and C) Loss are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.
rel: Other synonyms: attainment, success, feat. Antonym: failure (see sa-21).

question: Choose the synonym of DANGER.
reason: Danger means the possibility of harm, i.e. risk.
why: Danger means the chance of harm; its synonym is Risk. A) Shelter, B) Safety and D) Security are wrong: they mean being protected, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: hazard, peril, threat. Antonym: safety (see sa-26).

question: Choose the synonym of DETERMINATION.
reason: Determination means firmness of purpose, i.e. resolution.
why: Determination means firm decision to do something; its synonym is Resolution. A) Weakness, B) Hesitation and C) Doubt are wrong: they show lack of firmness, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: resolve, firmness, willpower. A New Year resolution is a firm decision to do something.

question: Choose the synonym of EFFICIENCY.
reason: Efficiency means the ability to work well, i.e. capability.
note: Fixed: source line 'Efficiency, capability' (comma instead of full stop).
why: Efficiency means ability to do work well; its synonym is Capability. B) Inability, C) Idleness and D) Weakness are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.
rel: Other synonyms: competence, effectiveness, potency (see sa-45). Antonym: inefficiency.

question: Choose the synonym of APPROVAL.
reason: Approval means agreeing to something, i.e. consent.
why: Approval means agreeing or giving permission; its synonym is Consent. B) Rejection, C) Denial and D) Refusal are wrong: they mean saying no, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: assent, sanction, permission. Antonym: disapproval (see sa-19).

question: Choose the synonym of AFFECTION.
reason: Affection means a feeling of fondness, i.e. love.
why: Affection means a feeling of liking and care; its synonym is Love. A) Anger, B) Dislike and C) Hatred are wrong: they are negative feelings, opposite to affection.
rel: Other synonyms: fondness, warmth, tenderness. Do not confuse affection (love) with affectation (showing off).

question: Choose the synonym of ABUSE.
reason: Abuse means insulting or harsh words, similar to reproach.
why: Abuse means harsh insulting words; its synonym is Reproach (blame, disgrace). A) Respect, B) Praise and C) Honour are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.
rel: Other synonyms: insult, censure, scolding. Antonym: commendation (see sa-31).

question: Choose the synonym of DISCLOSE.
reason: Disclose means to make known, i.e. reveal.
why: Disclose means to make known a secret; its synonym is Reveal. B) Hide, C) Cover and D) Conceal are wrong: they mean keep secret, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: expose, divulge, uncover. Antonyms: conceal, hide.

question: Choose the synonym of NEED.
reason: Need means a lack of something necessary, i.e. want.
why: Need means lack of something necessary; its synonym is Want. B) Surplus, C) Luxury and D) Plenty are wrong: they mean having more than enough, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: requirement, necessity, lack. Want also means need in sa-70.

question: Choose the synonym of LOWER.
reason: Lower means to reduce in value or dignity, i.e. debase.
why: Lower means to bring down in level or value; its synonym is Debase (lower in quality or worth). B) Elevate, C) Raise and D) Uplift are wrong: they mean to make higher, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: degrade, reduce, diminish. Antonyms: raise, elevate.

question: Choose the synonym of WANT.
reason: Want means lack of something required, i.e. need.
why: Want means lack or need of something; its synonym is Need. A) Wealth, B) Comfort and C) Excess are wrong: they mean having plenty, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: lack, poverty, shortage. Antonym: prosperity (see sa-32).

question: Choose the synonym of PROGRESS.
reason: Progress means forward movement, i.e. advance.
why: Progress means moving forward; its synonym is Advance. B) Regress, C) Decline and D) Retreat are wrong: they mean going back or getting worse, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: develop, proceed, improve. Antonym: retrogress (see sa-39).

question: Choose the synonym of SHY.
reason: Shy means timid in front of others, i.e. bashful.
why: Shy means nervous with other people; its synonym is Bashful. A) Confident, C) Outgoing and D) Bold are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.
rel: Other synonyms: timid, reserved, coy. Antonyms: bold, confident.

question: Choose the synonym of HUMBLE.
reason: Humble means modest and not proud, similar to meek.
why: Humble means modest, not proud; its synonym is Meek (quiet and gentle). A) Proud, B) Vain and C) Arrogant are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.
rel: Other synonyms: modest, unassuming, simple. Antonym: vain (see sa-7).

question: Choose the synonym of NERVOUS.
reason: Nervous means easily frightened or anxious, similar to timorous.
why: Nervous means fearful and worried; its synonym is Timorous (full of fear). A) Bold, B) Calm and D) Brave are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.
rel: Other synonyms: anxious, timid, uneasy. Antonym: bold (see sa-11).

question: Choose the synonym of TROTH.
reason: Troth is an old word for a pledge of loyalty, i.e. faith.
why: Troth is an old word meaning faith, loyalty or a promise; so Faith is the synonym. A) Doubt, B) Betrayal and D) Treachery are wrong: they mean distrust or disloyalty, the opposite.
rel: Betroth (to promise in marriage) comes from troth. Other synonyms: fidelity, loyalty, pledge.

question: Choose the synonym of EQUAL.
reason: Equal means the same in amount or quality, similar to uniform.
why: Equal means the same in amount or level; Uniform (the same throughout) is the synonym. B) Different, C) Unequal and D) Uneven are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.
rel: Other synonyms: same, identical, even. Antonym: uneven (see sa-36).

question: Choose the synonym of OWN.
reason: Own (verb) means to admit something, i.e. acknowledge.
why: Here own means to admit; its synonym is Acknowledge. A) Disclaim, B) Reject and D) Deny are wrong: they mean refusing to accept, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: admit, confess, accept. Antonym: disclaim (see sa-35).

question: Choose the synonym of NEGLECT.
reason: Neglect means failure to give proper care, i.e. negligence.
why: Neglect means not giving proper care; its synonym is Negligence. A) Care, B) Attention and D) Diligence are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.
rel: Other synonyms: carelessness, disregard. Do not confuse negligent (careless) with negligible (very small).

question: Choose the synonym of GODLY.
reason: Godly means devoted to God, i.e. pious.
why: Godly means religious and devoted to God; its synonym is Pious. B) Wicked, C) Irreligious and D) Sinful are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.
rel: Other synonyms: devout, religious, saintly. Antonyms: ungodly, impious.

question: Choose the synonym of MOB.
reason: Mob means a large disorderly group of people, i.e. crowd.
why: A mob is a large, often disorderly, group of people; its synonym is Crowd. B) Loner, C) Few and D) Individual are wrong: they mean one or a small number of people.
rel: Other synonyms: throng, horde, multitude, rabble. Mob rule means rule by crowds, not by law.

question: Choose the synonym of MOAT.
reason: A moat is a deep water-filled trench around a castle, i.e. a ditch.
why: A moat is a deep ditch, usually filled with water, around a castle or fort; its synonym is Ditch. B) Hill and C) Mound are wrong: they are raised land, not dug land. D) Wall is wrong: a wall is built up, though a moat is often near one.
rel: Other synonyms: trench, channel. Do not confuse moat with mote (a tiny particle of dust).

question: Choose the synonym of DISPERSE.
reason: Disperse means to spread in different directions, i.e. scatter.
why: Disperse means to spread or send in different directions; its synonym is Scatter. A) Collect, C) Assemble and D) Gather are wrong: they mean bring together, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: spread, dissipate, disband. Police disperse a crowd. Antonyms: gather, collect.

question: Choose the synonym of INCREMENT.
reason: Increment means an increase or addition, i.e. increase.
why: Increment means an increase or addition, as in a salary increment; its synonym is Increase. A) Decrease, B) Decline and C) Reduction are wrong: they mean going down, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: addition, rise, gain. Antonym: decrement (a decrease).

question: Choose the synonym of RESCIND.
reason: Rescind means to take back or annul, i.e. cancel.
why: Rescind means to cancel a law, order or agreement; its synonym is Cancel. B) Enact, C) Approve and D) Confirm are wrong: they mean make or keep valid, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: revoke, repeal, annul, withdraw. Antonyms: enact, validate.

question: Choose the synonym of QUIT.
reason: Quit means to go away from or give up, i.e. leave.
why: Quit means to go away from or stop; its synonym is Leave. A) Stay, C) Join and D) Remain are wrong: they mean to continue or come in, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: depart, abandon, resign, give up. Quit India Movement means asking the British to leave India.

question: Choose the synonym of LAUD.
reason: Laud means to praise highly.
why: Laud means to praise highly; its synonym is Praise. B) Blame, C) Condemn and D) Criticize are wrong: they are opposite in meaning.
rel: Other synonyms: extol, acclaim, applaud. Laudable means worthy of praise.

question: Choose the synonym of LUCK.
reason: Luck means fortune or chance, similar to lot (one's fate).
why: Luck means what happens to a person by chance; Lot (fate, one's fortune in life) is the synonym. A) Effort, B) Plan and D) Labour are wrong: they mean things done on purpose by hard work, not chance.
rel: Other synonyms: fortune, fate, destiny, chance. Phrase: to be content with one's lot.

question: Choose the synonym of COLLAPSE.
reason: Collapse means to fall down or fail suddenly, i.e. break down.
why: Collapse means to fall down suddenly or fail; its synonym is Break down. A) Build up, B) Recover and D) Rise are wrong: they mean getting stronger or higher, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: fall, cave in, crumble, fail. A building or a system can collapse.

question: Choose the synonym of CURB.
reason: Curb means to control or limit, i.e. restrain.
why: Curb means to control or hold back; its synonym is Restrain. A) Release, B) Encourage and D) Free are wrong: they mean let go or push forward, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: check, control, limit, suppress. Example: curb your anger. Do not confuse with kerb (edge of a road).

question: Choose the synonym of FERVOUR.
reason: Fervour means intense passion, i.e. zeal.
why: Fervour means strong, warm feeling or enthusiasm; its synonym is Zeal. A) Indifference, B) Coldness and D) Apathy are wrong: they mean lack of interest, the opposite.
rel: Other synonyms: passion, ardour, enthusiasm. Adjectives: fervent, zealous.
